Parameter estimates with robust (Mplus MLR) standard errors

parameters.Rd

All free (and boundary-fixed) parameters of a model, with robust sandwich standard errors as Mplus ESTIMATOR = MLR.

Usage

parameters(object, ref = NULL, order = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted LCA, LPA, LCGA, GMM, multigroup or LTA model (latentmix).

ref

For an LTA, the reference class of the multinomial logits (default K).

order

For an LTA, a relabelling of the classes (class k of the table is class order[k] of the model), e.g. to match the labels of another program.

Value

A data frame with one row per parameter and columns kind (e.g. "probability", "threshold", "mean", "variance", "covariance", "class logit", "growth mean", "growth variance", "residual variance"), group (multigroup models only), class (0 for parameters shared by all classes), item, level (category or second variable), estimate, se, z and p.

Details

For an LCA, item-response probabilities (kind = "probability") are reported together with the logit thresholds they derive from ("threshold"); category codes are mapped back to factor labels. Class proportions are parameterised as multinomial logits against the last class ("class logit"). Tests of probabilities and variances against zero are not meaningful (they are not starred in lm_table()). With a complex survey design (cluster, strata) the standard errors are design-based (Mplus TYPE = MIXTURE COMPLEX).

For a multigroup model the table has a group column (group label): class logits (against the last class) and class probabilities per group, the group logit ("group logit", log of the group-size ratio against the last group, Mplus [cg#1]), and the measurement parameters of every group (identical across groups when invariant).

For an LTA (with or without covariates and distal outcomes, or from lta3step()) the table follows the Mplus parameterisation, with columns parameter (Mplus-style label, e.g. "[C2#1]", "C2#1 ON C1#2", "C1#1 ON X1", "C1#2: [A1$1]"), kind ("threshold", "distal mean", "initial intercept", "initial slope", "transition intercept", "transition shift", "transition slope", ...), wave, class, from (origin class of a transition parameter; 0 = all), item, term, estimate, se, z, p; ref sets the reference class of the logits (default: the last class).

See also

summary.latentmix(), lm_table() (what = "parameters"), itemprobs(), profilemeans(), growthparams()

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# every parameter of the 4-class ACE model with its robust (MLR) standard error
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)     # 4 ACE classes, as generated
#> Starting Julia ...
head(parameters(m))
#>          kind class           item      level   estimate          se          z
#> 1 class logit     1    (Intercept) vs class 4 1.73557448 0.169792750  10.221723
#> 2 class logit     2    (Intercept) vs class 4 0.63058808 0.213652268   2.951469
#> 3 class logit     3    (Intercept) vs class 4 0.45493369 0.199634527   2.278833
#> 4 probability     1  ace_emo_abuse          0 0.93938201 0.012157845  77.265506
#> 5 probability     1  ace_emo_abuse          1 0.06061799 0.012157845   4.985916
#> 6 probability     1 ace_phys_abuse          0 0.96455645 0.008441933 114.257765
#>              p
#> 1 1.584980e-24
#> 2 3.162661e-03
#> 3 2.267701e-02
#> 4 0.000000e+00
#> 5 6.166906e-07
#> 6 0.000000e+00
# }
